key_contributions: Unmerge tracking stack and constraint-safe merge rates for recursive, permuted SReT stages.
Stage-wise single-shot token reduction preserving fixed sequence length within recursions.
GPU and Raspberry Pi 5 measurements of memory, throughput and latency.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (post-training); ImageNet-1K evaluation
setup.benchmarks: ImageNet-1K top-1, peak activation memory, throughput, latency

claims.claim: Token merging recovers part of the throughput/memory cost recursion adds, at a 1.47 pp accuracy cost; throughput only improves at larger batch.
claims.regime: same SReT weights, with vs without merging
claims.evidence_quote: Benchmarked on ImageNet-1K, our selected configuration reduces top-1 accuracy by 1.47 percentage points. On the GPU, it reduces peak activation memory by 37.3% and 38.4% at batch sizes 1 and 16

limitations: Throughput drops 21.7% at batch size 1 on GPU; accuracy loss.
survey_notes: Systems note for vision looping: recursion's activation-memory and throughput overhead is a deployment cost; token reduction is one remedy (analogous to KV/compute reduction work in LMs).

title: REFINEPPO: Learning Continuous Control Policies by Iterative Action Refinement
relevance_reason: A shared refinement network repeatedly applied to the action proposal (output-space iteration, not hidden-state looping) inside PPO policies.
one_sentence: RefinePPO builds continuous actions through K residual corrections from a shared state-and-proposal-conditioned network; across 14 control tasks it matches or exceeds PPO and K=4 gives the best normalized return.
key_contributions: Iterative Action Refinement: shared network repeatedly corrects an action proposal.
Integration with PPO and ablations of refinement depth and step-coefficient schedules.

setup.model_sizes: actor two 128-unit hidden layers (baseline and refinement field)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: 14 benchmark control tasks (MuJoCo etc.), 6M steps

claims.claim: Return improves from K=1 (non-iterative) to K=4, the best average depth.
claims.regime: same architecture, varied K (FLOPs not matched)
claims.evidence_quote: Performance generally improves as the refinement depth increases from K = 1 to K = 4, with K = 4 achieving the highest average normalized return.

survey_notes: Output-space iterative refinement (like diffusion policies or TRM answer refinement) rather than latent looping; useful contrast to RD-VLA (2602.07845), which argues latent-space recurrence beats action-space refinement.

title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability
relevance_reason: Compares TRM, a depth-conditioned recursive transformer (DEPTH) and a simple weight-shared recursive transformer as small-data engineering surrogates.
one_sentence: Hardware-aware comparison of TRM, a simple recursive transformer and a proposed depth-conditioned recursive transformer for FEA surrogate modeling (package stress/warpage, Laplace capacitance field); depth-conditioned recursion is Pareto-best in accuracy vs params and FLOPs.
key_contributions: Recursive weight sharing as a remedy for overfitting in small-data engineering surrogates.
Pareto analysis of MRR vs FLOPs and vs parameters across seven model variants.
TRM found parameter- and FLOP-expensive and off the Pareto frontier in this setting.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: Stress10K, Warpage10K (FEA), PINN Laplace capacitance datasets
setup.baselines: TRM variants, simple recursion variants, depth-conditioned variants

claims.claim: TRM-style dual-latent recursion is parameter- and FLOP-expensive without matching accuracy; depth-conditioned recursion (depth injected as input, per-step loss) gives the best accuracy-per-parameter/FLOP.
claims.regime: Pareto comparison across variants (not single matched pair)
claims.evidence_quote: of TRM (M4,M5) is both parameter- and FLOP-expensive without a commensurate accuracy return.

survey_notes: Science/engineering niche: looping motivated by small-data overfitting rather than test-time compute. A counterpoint to TRM transfer: TRM's dual-latent recursion is not Pareto-efficient here.

title: Tiny Recursive Models for Solving the J2-Perturbed Lambert Problem
relevance_reason: TRM-style two-level weight-shared recursive solver refining a departure velocity via simulated J2 trajectories and tracking error.
one_sentence: TRM-PL applies a 2.3M-parameter recursive module in a two-level latent hierarchy to refine Lambert departure velocities under J2 perturbation, cutting median terminal-position error by orders of magnitude versus the Keplerian initial guess.
key_contributions: Recursive (TRM) neural solver for the perturbed Lambert boundary-value problem with simulator-in-the-loop correction.
Compares joint learning vs refinement-only training with velocity or position supervision; refinement-only is most reliable.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: Synthetic LEO and Jovian single/multi-revolution transfers

claims.claim: Position-supervised recursive refinement reduces median terminal error from 21.7 km to 0.027 km on single-rev LEO with a 2.3M model.
claims.regime: vs Keplerian initial guess (no matched neural baseline)
claims.evidence_quote: the position-supervised refinement variant reduces the median terminal-position error from 21.7 km to 0.027 km on single-revolution LEO, from 340.9 km to 0.31 km on multi-revolution LEO

survey_notes: Second TRM transfer to astrodynamics (same simulate-and-correct loop as TRC 2512.16824). No comparison with a non-recursive network of matched size.

title: Adaptive Depth and Expert Refinement for Efficient Speech Enhancement
relevance_reason: Parameter-shared progressive speech-enhancement block repeated with a learned hard early-exit controller and per-iteration routed residual adapters.
one_sentence: ADER repeats a shared enhancement block with an adaptive depth controller for hard early exit and a top-1 router choosing one lightweight residual adapter per iteration, cutting MP-SENet params 70.4% and average compute 51.3% at WB-PESQ 3.37.
key_contributions: Adaptive Depth Controller for input-dependent number of shared refinement iterations.
Conditional Expert Router: per-iteration top-1 residual adapter selection (relaxed sharing).
Exit-aware intermediate supervision on randomly sampled iterations.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: VCTK-DEMAND

claims.claim: Shared iterative refinement with adaptive exit and routed adapters cuts parameters 70.4% and average compute 51.3% relative to MP-SENet while reaching WB-PESQ 3.37.
claims.regime: vs unshared MP-SENet baseline (different params and compute)
claims.evidence_quote: On VCTK-DEMAND, ADER reduces the parameter count and average computation of MP-SENet by 70.4% and 51.3%, respectively, while achieving a WB-PESQ of 3.37.

survey_notes: Speech example of looping plus per-iteration MoE adapters plus learned halting (cf. MoR, MoEUT in LMs).

title: Exploring the Hierarchical Reasoning Model for Small Natural-Image Classification Without Augmentation
relevance_reason: Evaluates HRM (two recurrent Transformer modules, one-step gradient, deep supervision) as an image classifier.
one_sentence: HRM trained on MNIST/CIFAR without augmentation optimizes stably but overfits natural images: 65.0% on CIFAR-10 vs 77.2% for a small CNN, and 29.7% vs 45.3% on CIFAR-100.
key_contributions: Negative result: HRM's recurrent reasoning lacks image inductive bias in the raw small-image regime.
Loss/error analysis showing healthy optimization but poor generalization.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, no augmentation

claims.claim: HRM is not competitive with a simple CNN on small natural images without augmentation and trains ~30x slower per epoch.
claims.regime: unmatched (different architectures; same data and optimizer family)
claims.evidence_quote: on CIFAR10, HRM reaches 65.0% after 25 epochs, whereas a two-stage Conv–BN–ReLU baseline attains 77.2% while training ∼ 30× faster per epoch

limitations: No augmentation, small scale; does not test modified HRM variants.
survey_notes: Negative transfer data point: HRM-style recurrence does not substitute for vision inductive biases (overfits). Contrast with looped ViTs that start from ViT/CNN backbones.

title: Semantic Communication with Memory
relevance_reason: Uses a Universal Transformer encoder as semantic transceiver for QA over noisy channels; looping is incidental, not studied.
one_sentence: Mem-DeepSC builds a semantic-communication QA system with a Universal-Transformer transceiver and a memory module, plus dynamic transmission masking; it beats benchmarks in answer accuracy and symbols transmitted.
key_contributions: Universal Transformer based semantic encoder/decoder with memory module for context.
Dynamic transmission by masking unessential elements via mutual-information training.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: Question-answer memory task over simulated channels

claims.claim: The UT-based Mem-DeepSC beats benchmark systems on answer accuracy and transmission efficiency; recurrence itself is not ablated.
claims.evidence_quote: Numerical results show that the proposed MemDeepSC is superior to benchmarks in terms of answer accuracy and transmission efficiency, i.e., number of transmitted symbols.

survey_notes: Peripheral: UT used as an off-the-shelf encoder in communications; no evidence about looping per se.

title: ACORT: A Compact Object Relation Transformer for Parameter Efficient Image Captioning
relevance_reason: Cross-layer (ALBERT-style) and attention parameter sharing to compress an image-captioning Transformer; looping only as compression.
one_sentence: ACORT combines radix encoding, cross-layer parameter sharing and attention parameter sharing to shrink an object-relation captioning Transformer 3.7x-21.6x without losing CIDEr on MS-COCO.
key_contributions: Cross-layer parameter sharing for captioning Transformers.
Attention parameter sharing and radix encoding for vocabulary.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: MS-COCO
setup.baselines: Object Relation Transformer baseline, SOTA captioners

claims.claim: Combined sharing methods give 3.7x-21.6x fewer parameters than the baseline without hurting test performance.
claims.regime: same depth/compute as baseline (iso-effective-depth), fewer params
claims.evidence_quote: By combining these methods, our proposed ACORT models have 3.7× to 21.6× fewer parameters than the baseline model without compromising test performance.

survey_notes: Compression-only use of cross-layer sharing in multimodal captioning; no test-time scaling.

title: Universal Transformer Hawkes Process with Adaptive Recursive Iteration
relevance_reason: Universal Transformer (recursion with adaptive halting) applied to neural Hawkes point processes for asynchronous event sequences.
one_sentence: UTHP replaces the stacked encoder of the Transformer Hawkes Process with a Universal Transformer with adaptive recursive iteration and CNN feed-forward, reporting modest gains over prior state of the art on event-sequence datasets.
key_contributions: Universal Transformer with ACT-style adaptive recursion for point processes.
CNN in position-wise feed-forward for local perception.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: Several asynchronous event-sequence datasets
setup.baselines: Transformer Hawkes Process, RNN point processes

claims.claim: Adding recursion (UT) to Transformer Hawkes processes gives a certain improvement over previous state of the art.
claims.evidence_quote: These experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that the performance of our proposed new model has a certain improvement compared with the previous state-of-the-art models.

survey_notes: Science/temporal point process application of UT with adaptive halting; weak regime control.

title: Residual Attention Net for Superior Cross-Domain Time Sequence Modeling
relevance_reason: Merges Universal Transformer with residual and highway nets for time-series classification; looping is a component, not analyzed.
one_sentence: RAN combines a Universal Transformer, residual net and highway connections for UCR time-series classification, reporting 35 state-of-the-art results out of 85 datasets.
key_contributions: Universal Transformer plus ResNet plus highway architecture for sequences.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: 85 UCR time-series datasets
setup.baselines: Prior UCR state of the art

claims.claim: RAN reaches 35 state-of-the-art and 10 matched results on 85 UCR datasets; recurrence not ablated.
claims.evidence_quote: Out of the standard 85 UCR data sets, we have achieved 35 state-of-the-art results with 10 results matching current state-of-the-art results without further model fine-tuning.

survey_notes: Peripheral time-series application of UT; proof-of-concept, no loop analysis.

title: Recursive Vision Transformer with Dynamic Depth and Width Adjustment for Resource-Efficient Image Semantic Communication
relevance_reason: Recursive ViT encoder for image semantic communication with content/channel-adaptive number of recursive modules and dynamic width.
one_sentence: A recursive ViT for wireless image semantic communication iteratively refines features with shared modules, with dynamic depth (number of recursions from image content and channel SNR) and dynamic width pruning; it cuts parameters 48.7% at comparable complexity.
key_contributions: Recursive ViT transceiver reducing parameters.
Dynamic depth, dynamic width and joint width-depth adjustment.
